title: Origami subnet orchestrator: terraform module for multi-tier subnets, NAT/IGW, endpoints and routing
creator: Harini Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (origami-subnet-orchestrator) that provisions opinionated multi-tier VPC topology for Redwood Private deployments. The module will create AZ-aware public/private/utility subnets, attach IGW and managed NATs with autoscaling patterns, create interface and gateway VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, STS, KMS, SSM), manage route tables with explicit egress routes, and expose hooks for safe in-place upgrades and health probes. The goal is a production-ready, testable module that enforces security defaults, supports canary upgrades of route/endpoint changes, and provides automated health checks and self-healing remediation via a non-destructive terraform workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module outputs a consistent set of subnet IDs and route table IDs per AZ for both public and private tiers
Module toggles between managed NAT Gateway pool and customer-provided NAT instances via variable without resource drift
VPC endpoints created idempotently with policy attachments; endpoints for S3 are gateway endpoints, others are interface endpoints with security group bindings
Automated health probes (lambda) verify NAT egress, endpoint reachability, and route table consistency after apply; probes report to a CloudWatch dashboard and a sample runbook
Upgrade hooks: plan-phase validations catch destructive route replacements and require explicit opt-in variable to perform in-place replacement
Conformance tests: terraform plan/apply in CI (successful and drift scenarios) plus unit tests with terratest for AZ failure simulation
Module passes security review checklist (KMS in use for sensitive endpoints, least-privilege IAM for created resources)
notes: We are standardizing on explicit route table attachments per subnet (no implicit default route table reliance)
Decision: prefer provider-managed NAT Gateway pool for most customers, but keep option for NAT instances for constrained on-prem infra
Edge case: accounts with existing IGW/NAT resources will be supported via import guidance and a migration plan in the runbook
